title: When reuse catches up
hook: €12 once or €0.20 each use: when do their modeled costs per use match?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Find a reuse cost-per-use crossover under explicitly limited costs.

misconception: A reusable purchase is automatically cheaper at every use count.
objective: Find a reuse cost-per-use crossover under explicitly limited costs.

claims.text: A reusable item costs €12 once. Equivalent single-use items cost €0.20 each. Ongoing costs are excluded. Scaled model; fictional prices; upkeep excluded; equivalent service.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Uses=50, A=0.24€/use and B=0.2€/use. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",12,"x"]; B=0.2; x denotes Uses. At x=50, A=0.24, B=0.2. The equality milestone requires x=60, where both are 0.2€/use; the slider then stays at this observed state. Transfer recall: €18÷€0.20/use=90 uses. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Divide a one-time amount by uses to obtain its modeled cost per use. Here it matches €0.20 at sixty uses. This omits upkeep, lifespan and environmental impacts and makes no purchasing recommendation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",12,"x"]; B=0.2; x denotes Uses. At x=50, A=0.24, B=0.2. The equality milestone requires x=60, where both are 0.2€/use; the slider then stays at this observed state. Transfer recall: €18÷€0.20/use=90 uses. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A reusable item costs €15 once; equivalent single-use items cost €0.25 each; ongoing costs are excluded. At how many uses do their costs per use match? Correct: 60. €15 ÷ uses = €0.25 when uses = 60; below that, the reusable item costs more per use in this model.
claims.source: Equality in the fresh recall scenario: €18/use-count = €0.20/use, so use-count = 18÷0.20 = 90. Ongoing costs, useful life and environmental impacts are excluded. In the stage, the €12 version matches at 60 uses and the reveal is gated on observing that exact equality. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.
